plan: Store the constructor's dict as a single deep-copied internal tree; to_data() deep-copies it back out so external mutation can never touch internal state.

Implement one recursive depth-first generator over (item, depth) pairs; total_word_count, unresolved_markers, and outline are each a single pass over it, guaranteeing deterministic list-order traversal.

Count note words by first deleting every `[[?identifier]]` token (regex `\[\[\?(\w+)\]\]`, replaced with a space so deletion cannot fuse adjacent words) and then counting `\b\w+\b` matches; add each reference's declared word_count.
Collect unresolved identifiers from note marker tokens and reference `unresolved` lists into a set, returned sorted lexicographically.
Render the outline as the workspace title followed by '  ' * depth + '<kind>: <title>' per item, with top-level items at depth 1.

For move, run every validation before any mutation: both ids must be strings; the item must exist; the destination must be the literal 'workspace' or an existing section/group; index (when given) must be an int in 0..len(destination); the destination must not be the item itself or inside its subtree. Only then remove the node from its parent list and insert/append it, so a failed move provably leaves to_data() unchanged and a successful one moves the intact subtree.
mechanisms: single deep-copied dict tree as sole state
set-based marker aggregation with sorted output
validate-before-mutate move with subtree containment check
